title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA LAUNCHES BRAHMA KUMARIS’ CAMPAIGN ‘SPIRITUAL AWAKENING FOR WORLD RENEWAL’ AND INAUGURATES ‘GLOBAL SPIRITUAL PALACE’ RETREAT CENTRE AT VADODARA, GUJARAT
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu launched Brahma Kumaris’ campaign ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurated the ‘Global Spiritual Palace’ Retreat Centre at Vadodara, Gujarat today (September 23, 2026). On the occasion, the President also virtually launched the campaign ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ of Brahma Kumaris Nadiad, Gujarat.
Addressing the gathering, the President said that today, there is a need not only for economic development but also for human development. We need an education that does not merely develop the intellect but also awakens wisdom. We need progress that is accompanied by sensitivity towards nature. We need a form of strength that teaches self-control rather than the control of others. We need spirituality that connects human beings. She was happy to note that the Brahma Kumaris organisation has spread the message of personal transformation and global renewal, through meditation and spiritual knowledge, not only across India but also to many countries around the world.
The President said that the potential for change exists within every human being. If people believe that changing their thoughts and actions can transform their life and if hope and self-respect are restored to them, they can become instruments of positive change not only for themselves but for society as a whole. She expressed confidence that today's inauguration of the Global Spiritual Palace will become a place where people from diverse sections of society can come together in peace and harmony.
The President said that it is heartening to virtually inaugurate the ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat: Awakening Inner Strength for Nation Building’ campaign at Nadiad, the birthplace of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. She said that when the youth channel their thoughts, emotions, and actions in a positive direction, the impact extends to the family, the workplace, the community, and ultimately, the entire nation. Therefore, "Awakening Inner Strength" is not merely a message of personal development but a profound process of nation-building. She emphasised that it is our collective responsibility to empower the youth. We have to transform them into self-reliant, peace-loving and responsible citizens.
The President said that self-transformation is considered the foundation of societal transformation. Today, there is a need to align this great legacy with the requirements of modern life. Our goal should be to build an India that is economically prosperous, scientifically advanced, socially inclusive, and spiritually awakened.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE 75TH ANNUAL CONVOCATION CEREMONY OF MAHARAJA SAYAJIRAO UNIVERSITY OF BARODA
subtitle: EDUCATION WILL BE MEANINGFUL IF IT BENEFITS THE COUNTRY AND THE SOCIETY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the 75th annual convocation ceremony of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda at Vadodara, Gujarat today (September 23, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that from the past 75 years, the university has been advancing by integrating diverse streams of knowledge.
The President underlined that in today's world, the solution to any problem is not confined to a single discipline. She emphasised that a multidisciplinary approach is necessary to address the critical challenges. We need the curiosity of a scientist, the sensitivity of an artist, the perspective of a historian, the insight of an economist, and the consciousness of a sociologist. She stated that higher education institutions like Maharaja Sayajirao University are expected to remain constantly alert and dynamic in this direction.
The President asked graduating students to reflect on the purpose of their education and knowledge. She said that when they move ahead in their professional field by prioritizing the interests of the nation and society, they will also progress, and that progress will bring them immense satisfaction.
The President said that education will be meaningful only if it benefits the country and society. She advised students that as engineers, they should develop technologies that improve people's lives; as doctors, they should view medicine not merely as a profession but as a form of service; as scientists, they should find solutions to problems in the interest of humanity; as artists or writers, they should enrich the sensitivity of society; as entrepreneurs, they should create not just wealth, but also employment and opportunities; as teachers, they should focus on nurturing a young generation that embraces both heritage and progress; and in public life, they should regard their position as a responsibility rather than a source of authority.
The President said that we are moving forward with the national goal of building Viksit Bharat by the year 2047 - a country where quality education and healthcare facilities reach everyone; where science and technology are utilized for human welfare; where there is equality of opportunity; where the full potential of women and the youth is harnessed; and a Bharat where every citizen has the opportunity to live a life of dignity. She said that universities and youth have to play an important role in achieving these goals.

title: AIIA Celebrates 11th Ayurveda Day–2026 with Public Awareness Rally, Seminar and Book Launches
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, celebrated the 11th Ayurveda Day at its campus with a series of academic, awareness and outreach activities. Two major programmes were organised as part of the celebrations.
To mark the occasion, an “Ayurveda Public Awareness Rally” was organised in the morning with the objective of promoting Ayurveda, propagating its principles, and creating greater public awareness about the role of Ayurveda in healthy living and holistic healthcare.
Prof. (Vaidya) P.K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, participated in the rally along with Prof. (Dr.) Manjusha Rajagopala, Dean, DU; Prof. (Dr.) Mahesh Vyas, Dean, Ph.D.; Prof. (Dr.) Ramakant Yadav, Dean, PG; Dr. Yogesh Badwe, MS; and faculty members, non-faculty members, Ph.D. and postgraduate (PG) scholars, and staff of the Institute.
In the afternoon, a seminar was organised on the theme “One Health, One Future: Integrating Science through Evidence, Innovations & Holistic Care.” Prof. (Dr.) Ravichandiran V., Vice-Chancellor, Delhi Pharmaceutical Sciences and Research University (DPSRU), was the Chief Guest at the programme. He congratulated AIIA for its efforts towards promoting Ayurveda globally and appreciated the Institute’s initiatives. Dr. Vinay Choudhary, Medical Officer, Department of AYUSH, Government of India, was the Guest of Honour. He delivered a lecture on autoimmune disorders in clinical Ayurvedic practice.
Prof. (Vaidya) Pradeep Kumar Prajapati, Director, AIIA, emphasised the importance of collective participation in Ayurveda awareness initiatives and strengthening public engagement with Ayurveda as part of the Institute’s outreach activities. Speaking on the occasion, he highlighted the various initiatives undertaken by AIIA to mark Ayurveda Day. He said, “In line with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, One Earth, One Health, Ayurveda is today moving beyond being India’s traditional healthcare heritage to become an important part of the global health discourse. As part of these celebrations, departments have organised seminars, expert lectures, webinars, public awareness programmes and patient-centric activities on diverse aspects of Ayurveda and healthcare.”
He also informed that AIIA launched “AyurVarta,” a special talk show dedicated to Ayurveda. The Institute organised AYURPRABHA-2026, a six-day workshop on Ayurveda Dermatology and Cosmetology, and conducted a special eye-screening camp for students of an NTPC school, among several other initiatives.
Two books, “Tarangini Sara Sangraha” and “Integrative Healthcare for Better Outcomes,” were also launched on the occasion.

title: CARI Guwahati Concludes 10-Day Celebrations of 11th Ayurveda Day
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 8:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), Guwahati, concluded a 10-day series of programmes organised to mark the 11th Ayurveda Day 2026 with a public walkathon today.
Held under the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”, the celebrations included health camps, awareness programmes, lectures, exhibitions and community outreach activities focused on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle practices and Ayurveda.
As part of the celebrations, CARI Guwahati organised free health check-up camps at various locations across Assam, providing medical consultations, diagnostic screenings and Ayurvedic medicines. The camps also focused on creating awareness about early intervention and preventive healthcare practices.
Awareness lectures were organised at the Institute’s OPD on various aspects of Ayurveda, including Dinacharya (daily regimen), Ritucharya (seasonal regimen) and appropriate Ahara (diet). Interactive exhibitions and awareness activities on medicinal plants were also organised to familiarise the public with their traditional uses and importance.
CARI Guwahati also conducted outreach programmes for personnel of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) at IOCL, Bongaigaon, focusing on stress management, yoga and Ayurveda-based approaches for maintaining physical and mental well-being.
An expert seminar on Marma Chikitsa was conducted by Dr. Tikendrajit Sarma, Associate Professor, Government Ayurvedic College, Guwahati. The session provided an overview of traditional Ayurvedic approaches related to Marma points and their relevance in healthcare.
Speaking on the occasion, Dr. P. L. Bharati, Research Officer (In-charge), CARI Guwahati, highlighted the role of Ayurveda in promoting preventive healthcare and healthy living. He said that the 10-day programme was aimed at connecting Ayurvedic principles with contemporary lifestyle needs and encouraging people to adopt healthy practices in their daily lives.
The celebrations culminated in a public walkathon, which was flagged off by Mrs. Anjana Bora, Councillor, Ward No. 43, Guwahati Municipal Corporation. Healthcare professionals, youth and members of the local community participated in the event.
The 10-day celebrations provided a platform for CARI Guwahati to engage with the community through healthcare services, awareness activities and educational programmes, highlighting the preventive and promotive aspects of Ayurveda.

title: 11th Ayurveda Day Celebrated at Regional Ayurveda Research Institute, Mandi After Month-Long Awareness Campaign
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI), Mandi, celebrated the 11th Ayurveda Day on September 23, 2026, with enthusiasm and participation following a month-long public awareness campaign organised on the theme “Ayurveda for a Healthy Tomorrow”.
During September, the Institute organised a series of awareness activities covering important aspects of Ayurveda, including evidence-based and safe treatment practices, healthy digestion and diet, safe use of medicines, prevention of lifestyle disorders, mental health, Ritucharya and research ethics. Senior Research Fellows (SRFs) and consultants of the Institute delivered a series of lectures on these topics, benefiting hundreds of people.
To encourage interest in Ayurveda among students, the Institute organised poster-making, slogan-writing, essay-writing and rangoli competitions. A Prakriti Assessment Camp was also organised on September 11, 2026, in which 45 beneficiaries were provided guidance on Ayurvedic diet and lifestyle based on their individual Prakriti, health and sleep-related aspects.
As part of the awareness campaign, a Walkathon was organised on September 22 from the Institute premises to BBMB Colony. Around 60 people, including school students and Institute personnel, participated in the awareness walk.
The month-long campaign culminated in the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations at the Institute on September 23. The day began with Havan and Pujan, followed by distribution of medicinal plants. The main programme commenced with the lighting of the ceremonial lamp by Dr. Vineeta Kumari Negi, In-charge, RARI Mandi, before the idol of Lord Dhanvantari, followed by the singing of the CCRAS Kulgeet.
Welcoming principals, teachers from nearby schools and other distinguished guests, Dr. Vineeta Kumari Negi extended greetings on Ayurveda Day. In her address, she highlighted the importance of holistic well-being through the principles of Ayurveda and emphasised the relevance of adopting an Ayurvedic lifestyle for building a healthy and prosperous future.
The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Vikas Nargiyal, Nodal Officer for the event. He expressed gratitude to all teachers, principals and Institute personnel for their valuable contribution towards the successful organisation of the month-long campaign and Ayurveda Day celebrations.

Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Ministry of Ayush, organised the inaugural programme of the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026, highlighting the importance of dietary diversity, healthy eating practices and adequate protein intake. Organised under the aegis of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, the programme focused on informed dietary choices and adequate nutrition.
A nutrition pledge was administered during the programme under the leadership of Dr. Jyoti Keswani, Director (Additional Charge), MDNIY and Chief Patron of the event. Dr. Keswani highlighted the importance of greater public awareness about nutritious dietary practices and healthy lifestyles.
An expert lecture on “Dietary Diversity and Adequate Protein” was delivered by Dr. Swati Jain, Scientist ‘D’, ICMR-National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research (ICMR-NICPR). She emphasised that protein adequacy should be considered as part of a balanced and diverse diet.
Dr. Jain highlighted the role of protein in tissue repair, immunity, muscle maintenance and the production of enzymes and hormones. Referring to the ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements for Indians, she noted that the safe protein allowance for healthy adults is 0.83 g per kg body weight per day when the diet contains high-quality protein, and 1.0 g per kg per day for predominantly cereal-based diets with lower protein quality. She also noted that protein requirements vary with age, body size, physiological state, physical activity and health status.
Emphasising dietary diversity, Dr. Jain encouraged inclusion of pulses, dairy, soy, nuts and seeds along with cereals. She cited traditional food combinations such as dal-rice, roti-chana, idli-sambar, dosa-sambar and khichdi as practical examples of complementary protein sources. She also highlighted affordable protein-containing foods such as sattu, dal, roasted chana, peanuts and soy.
Dr. Jain noted that protein intake should be distributed across meals rather than concentrated in a single meal. For individuals practising Yoga, she emphasised that overall daily protein intake and a balanced diet are more important than focusing exclusively on a post-exercise “protein window”.
The programme was coordinated by Dr. Khushbu Jain, Assistant Professor (Biochemistry), MDNIY, and conducted by Dr. Pawan Kumar, Assistant Professor (Yoga Education).

content:
The 11th Ayurveda Day was celebrated with enthusiasm across India and the world. The grand national celebrations were held in Nagpur, Maharashtra. This year’s theme was “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow (स्वस्थ भविष्य के लिए आयुर्वेद)”. The programme witnessed the unveiling of key reports and documents, including the report on the Ayush Services Sector and “Ayush Vision 2030”, along with the launch of the CCRAS–AGNI Web Portal. The event also featured scientific sessions on Ayurveda’s role in healthcare and public health, as well as the roadmap towards 2047.
Hon'ble Prime Minister’s message on the occasion was read out during the programme. In his message, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi said that Ayurveda’s journey from tradition to knowledge, evidence and innovation will contribute to securing the health and wellbeing of future generations. He highlighted that Ayurveda’s identity has expanded beyond India’s borders, with the Ayush Visa facility enabling foreign nationals to seek treatment under Ayush systems in India. Referring to the resolve of ‘Shakti ki Sadhna’, the Prime Minister said that India is moving steadily towards a Viksit Bharat and expressed confidence that institutions, experts and youth associated with Ayurveda will take this rich tradition to new heights and contribute to building a healthy, capable and strong nation.
The celebration ceremony was virtually inaugurated by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav in the presence of Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Director General, Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS), Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, and other dignitaries.
Addressing the celebration, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav described Ayurveda as a key part of India's health vision, saying, "स्वास्थ्य का पहला केंद्र अस्पताल नहीं, हमारा घर है। स्वास्थ्य का पहला आधार दवा नहीं, हमारी जीवनशैली है।" Citing the principle "स्वस्थस्य स्वास्थ्य रक्षणम्, आतुरस्य विकार प्रशमनम्", he said Ayurveda prioritises preserving health alongside treatment, an approach he called increasingly relevant amid rising lifestyle-related health concerns.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav cited the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, ITRA Jamnagar's recognition as an Institute of National Importance, and the inclusion of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani in the WHO ICD-11 classification as key steps in internationalising traditional medicine. He called for connecting tradition with knowledge, evidence and innovation, adding that Ayurveda Day should extend beyond an annual observance to drive wider public engagement on healthy living.
Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, emphasised that the future of Ayurveda lies in connecting its knowledge tradition with scientific evidence, innovation and public health outcomes. He stressed the need to strengthen research, quality, safety and standardisation while promoting collaboration between Ayurveda and other healthcare systems. Highlighting key developments including the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, more than 43,000 research publications on the Ayush Research Portal, over 200 BIS standards and the Ayush Quality Mark, he said these efforts are aimed at making Ayush systems more scientific, evidence-based and globally relevant.
The programme witnessed the launch of Safety Dossiers on Gokshura (Tribulus terrestris) and Chandrasura (Lepidium sativum), Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs) on Skin Disorders, and the first-ever Report on the “Ayush Services Sector”, prepared by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS), providing an assessment of the Ayush services sector.
The event also saw the launch of “From Traditional Wisdom to Global Leadership: Ayush Vision 2030”, the Status Report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, and the CCRAS–AGNI Assessment Scale Web Portal. The initiatives focus on strengthening research, documentation, innovation, clinical guidance and the systematic translation of Ayurveda knowledge into practice.
The programme also featured the presentation of Ayush Quality Mark Certification to four eligible industries by the Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, reflecting the emphasis on quality and standardisation within the Ayush sector.
The celebrations featured two scientific sessions on the evolving role of Ayurveda in healthcare and public health. The first session, “Shashwatam to Vishwas – Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow and the Road to 2047”, featured Dr. G. Geethakrishnan Pillai, Unit Head, WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre, Jamnagar, and focused on the future trajectory of Ayurveda, evidence generation and its role in the broader health vision towards 2047.  The second session, “Integrating Therapies is needed to reduce NCD Burden by 2027”, featured Dr. Shiv Kumar Sarin, Director, Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences (ILBS), New Delhi, and deliberated on the potential of integrated therapeutic approaches in addressing the growing burden of non-communicable diseases.
The scientific deliberations were followed by a summary presented by Prof. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice Chancellor, National Institute of Ayurveda, Jaipur. Prof. (Dr.) Unnat P. Pandit, Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trade Marks, also delivered remarks on the report on Ayush-related Inventions in India, while Dr. A. Raghu, Adviser (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush, spoke on the Standard Treatment Guidelines on Skin Disorders.
The event was graced by Shri Satyajit Paul, Senior Statistical Advisor, Ministry of Ayush; and Prof. Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS) along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush, representatives of Ayush Councils and institutions.
A National Medicinal Plants Exhibition was also set up at the venue, featuring stalls by national institutions under the Ministry of Ayush and attracting considerable interest among visitors and participants.
The national celebration in Nagpur brought together practitioners, researchers, scientists, academics, institutions and other stakeholders from across the country, highlighting the growing focus on evidence, research, innovation, quality and holistic care in advancing Ayurveda.

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, will undertake Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026, with a focus on institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency, strengthening record management, promoting responsible e-waste disposal and ensuring optimum utilisation of office space across the Department and its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations.
The campaign will be implemented in two phases. The Preparatory Phase, being undertaken from 15th to 30th September 2026, focuses on identification of targets, review of records and pending references, and preparations for cleanliness drives and disposal activities during the main campaign period.
Special Campaign 6.0 aims to achieve saturation of Swachhata across the office premises of DPIIT and its attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations, including their field and branch offices located across the country. The campaign will cover all 19 attached, subordinate and autonomous organisations under the administrative control of DPIIT.
DPIIT had participated extensively in Special Campaign 5.0 and achieved significant outcomes in cleanliness, record management, pendency reduction and space utilisation. During the campaign, 1,572 physical files were reviewed, of which 1,119 files were weeded out in accordance with applicable record-retention procedures. Disposal of obsolete records and scrap resulted in the release of 11,235 square feet of office space and revenue generation of ₹17,69,569.
The Department also addressed its identified pendency targets, including disposal of Public Grievances and Public Grievance Appeals, as well as identified areas for simplification of rules and procedures. These initiatives contributed to improving efficiency, responsiveness and the overall work experience of officials and staff.
Building on these outcomes, Special Campaign 6.0 will place greater emphasis on sustainable cleanliness practices, systematic record management and efficient utilisation of government office space. The key areas of focus will include saturation of Swachhata in office premises and surrounding areas; identification and disposal of pending references within prescribed timelines; review and weeding out of records as per applicable record-retention schedules; effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste through authorised channels; disposal of obsolete and unserviceable items and scrap; optimum utilisation and release of office space; improvement of workplace aesthetics, cleanliness and functionality; and institutionalisation of sustainable and environmentally responsible practices.

This will facilitate environmentally sound disposal of obsolete electronic equipment while supporting cleaner and better-organised government workplaces.
The campaign will also encourage DPIIT's organisations to adopt innovative and replicable solutions that promote sustainability and the principles of a circular economy. An example in this regard is the “Waste to Wealth” initiative undertaken by the Indian Rubber Material Research Institute (IRMRI), an autonomous organisation under DPIIT. Under the initiative, discarded rubber scrap was utilised for construction of a road section and access road using Waste Rubber Tiles and Crumb Rubber Cement Concrete (CRCC), incorporating approximately 10–15 per cent waste rubber particles in the cement-concrete mix. The performance of the road was scientifically monitored for parameters including strength, elasticity and durability.
Such innovative practices will be encouraged during Special Campaign 6.0 for wider adoption and replication, wherever feasible.
Through Special Campaign 6.0, DPIIT and its organisations will make concerted efforts to further strengthen the culture of Swachhata, efficiency, accountability and good governance across their offices. The campaign will also seek to ensure that the outcomes achieved are sustained and institutionalised beyond the campaign period, contributing to cleaner, more efficient, sustainable and citizen-centric government workplaces.

title: Centre for Trade and Investment Law Hosts Webinar on WTO Fisheries Subsidies Agreement
subtitle: Experts Deliberate on WTO Fisheries Subsidies Pact, Implementation Challenges and Ongoing Negotiations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 11:58AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Centre for Trade and Investment Law (CTIL), Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, organised a webinar on “WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies: Legal Framework and Policy Prospects” on 21 September 2026. The webinar coincided with the commencement of WTO Fish Week and followed India’s ratification of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies (AFS) on 20 July 2026. International trade law experts, fisheries specialists and policymakers participated in discussions on implementation of the Agreement, one year after its entry into force, as well as ongoing negotiations on additional disciplines concerning overcapacity and overfishing.
The webinar highlighted the importance of reliable fisheries data, strengthened monitoring and reporting systems, institutional coordination and adequate technical capacity for effective implementation of the AFS. The need for continued capacity building and technical assistance for developing and least-developed Members, including through available WTO mechanisms, was also discussed.
The AFS, adopted at the WTO’s Twelfth Ministerial Conference in 2022, establishes disciplines on certain harmful fisheries subsidies, including subsidies linked to illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, fishing of overfished stocks, subject to specified rebuilding conditions, and fishing on the unregulated high seas. The Agreement also provides for notification and transparency obligations and requires Members that have accepted the Agreement to put in place measures for its implementation and administration, including steps to give effect to its substantive disciplines and comply with notification requirements.
The discussions covered implementation challenges, notification and transparency requirements, special and differential treatment (S&DT), domestic institutional preparedness, small-scale fisheries and ongoing negotiations on additional disciplines concerning overcapacity and overfishing.
The expert panel comprised Ms. Alice Tipping, Director, Trade and Sustainable Development, International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD), Geneva; Mr. Tristan Irschlinger, Senior Policy Advisor, IISD, Geneva; Prof. Mukesh Bhatnagar, Former Professor, Centre for WTO Studies (CWTOS); and Mr. Sebastian Mathew, Small-scale Fisheries Advisor. The session was moderated by Prof. James J. Nedumpara, Professor and Head, CTIL, and Head-in-Charge, CWTOS. Ms. Priyansha Hajela, Consultant (Legal), CTIL, delivered the opening remarks.
The panellists discussed the substantive disciplines and implementation of the AFS, including notification and transparency requirements, domestic data systems, inter-agency coordination and the relevance of India’s legal and policy framework. The deliberations also covered the negotiating history and ongoing negotiations on overcapacity and overfishing, the role of the IISD self-assessment toolkit in identifying implementation and capacity-building needs, and livelihood, food security and developmental concerns of small-scale and artisanal fisheries. Issues relating to vessel registration, monitoring and IUU-related determinations were also discussed.
The programme concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, during which participants engaged with the panellists on practical and legal aspects of implementing the AFS, including notification and transparency, IUU fishing, rebuilding of overfished stocks, S&DT and small-scale fisheries. The webinar highlighted the importance of continued dialogue and coordination among international organisations and fisheries stakeholders to strengthen domestic preparedness and support effective implementation of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.

Based on the principle of “Driver is the Owner”, Bharat Taxi will make Saarthis the real stakeholders of their own service through the cooperative model: Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol

More than 10 lakh Saarthis have joined Bharat Taxi in six months; around 20,000 rides being completed every day and more than Rs 100 crore credited to Saarthis’ accounts: Shri Mohol

Ministry of Cooperation has launched more than 160 new initiatives during the last five years: Shri Mohol

Computerisation of around 80,000 PACS underway across the country at a cost of approximately Rs 3,000 crore

Around 54 lakh new cooperative members enrolled in Uttar Pradesh; PACS membership campaign described as a model worth emulating across the country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership and guidance of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah, a series of significant initiatives have been undertaken over the past few years to make India’s cooperative sector modern, transparent, technology-enabled and multidimensional. Cooperation is steadily expanding beyond its traditional domains into agriculture, rural economy, organic products, seeds, exports, storage, healthcare services and now emerging sectors such as mobility. Taking this vision forward, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol today addressed the formal launch programme of Bharat Taxi in Lucknow. Along with Lucknow, the service was also launched today in Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Brajesh Pathak, Agriculture Minister Shri Surya Pratap Shahi, Cooperation Minister Shri J.P.S. Rathore, Transport Minister Shri Dayashankar Singh, Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Gram Vikas Bank Shri Vivek Singh Tomar, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Shri Pankaj Bansal, advisers to the Chief Minister, senior officers of the Uttar Pradesh Government, public representatives and a large number of Bharat Taxi Saarthis were present on the occasion. More than 50,000 people from different districts of Uttar Pradesh also joined the programme through the online mode.
During the programme, Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath launched the ‘Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana’ Portal. Along with this, the Urvarak Setu Mobile App, developed by the Cooperation Department of Uttar Pradesh, and the UPCDC Mobile App of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Database Centre were also launched. On the occasion, the Airport Authority, Lucknow Metro Rail and Lucknow Police exchanged Memoranda of Understanding with Bharat Taxi.
Recalling the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation in July 2021, Shri Mohol underlined that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s historic decision gave a new direction and renewed momentum to the cooperative movement in the country. Under the leadership of Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah, the Ministry of Cooperation has launched more than 160 new initiatives during the last five years, aimed at making cooperative institutions stronger, transparent, modern and economically capable. Highlighting the scale and reach of the movement, he noted that India today has around 8.5 lakh cooperative societies, with nearly 32 crore members associated with them, while the cooperative sector is presently active across around 30 different sectors.
Highlighting the technology-led transformation of grassroots cooperatives, Shri Mohol stated that the computerisation of around 80,000 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) is underway across the country at a cost of approximately Rs 3,000 crore. The role of PACS, he emphasised, is no longer confined to agricultural credit, agricultural inputs, sugar and dairy businesses. PACS are now being linked with several new areas, including foodgrain storage, insurance, organic products, indigenous seeds, Common Service Centres, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, Jan Aushadhi Kendras and petrol-diesel distribution. With the reform of the Model Bye-Laws of PACS, they can now undertake more than 25 different economic activities, creating new opportunities for employment and income generation at the village level.
Elaborating on the Government’s effort to bring the entire ‘seed-to-market’ value chain within the cooperative framework, the Union Minister of State for Cooperation referred to the establishment of new national-level multi-State cooperative societies in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s resolve of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’. These include Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) for quality seeds, National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) for organic products and National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) for promoting the export of cooperative products. Around 70,000 cooperative societies across the country have already become associated with these three organisations, directly benefiting farmers and cooperative institutions.
Highlighting the initiatives being taken in the dairy and human resource sectors, Shri Mohol stated that under White Revolution 2.0, efforts are underway to increase the country’s present milk production capacity by approximately 40 percent. At the same time, the country’s first cooperative university has been established to provide trained and capable human resources to cooperative institutions. Emphasising that a strong and transparent cooperative movement requires professionally trained youth, he said Tribhuvan Sahkari University will play an important role in developing nearly 17 lakh trained human resources for the cooperative sector in the coming years.
Illustrating the Central Government’s growing financial support to the cooperative movement, Shri Mohol highlighted the role of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). From its establishment in 1963 until 2014, over a period of nearly five decades, NCDC extended assistance of around Rs 45,000 crore to the cooperative sector, whereas during approximately the last 12 years, this assistance has increased to nearly Rs 4.5 lakh crore. He said this reflects the Central Government’s strong commitment towards financially strengthening the cooperative sector.
Referring to Bharat Taxi, Shri Mohol described it as an important new cooperative initiative in the mobility sector, built around the core principle “Driver is the Owner.” Explaining the significance of the model, he said the driver is not merely a service provider but also a stakeholder and owner in the cooperative ecosystem. Unlike conventional aggregator models, where drivers are required to pay a part of their earnings as commission, Bharat Taxi seeks to ensure that the maximum benefit from earnings goes directly to the Saarthis. Earnings from the service are credited directly to their accounts, while the cooperative structure also gives them a stake in ownership and participation in the decision-making process. Highlighting the rapid growth of the initiative since its launch in February 2026, he stated that more than 10 lakh Saarthis have joined Bharat Taxi within just six months and around 20,000 rides are being undertaken every day. Around 40 lakh passengers have also joined the service, while more than Rs 100 crore has been credited to the accounts of Saarthis during the last six months. Bharat Taxi is presently operating in various parts of the country, including Delhi, Gujarat, Mumbai, Jaipur and Chandigarh, and with the addition of Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj, its presence in Uttar Pradesh has expanded significantly. Around 40,000 Saarthi brothers and sisters have already registered across these five cities and will soon begin providing services to passengers.
Commending the development trajectory of Uttar Pradesh under Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Shri Mohol noted the State’s rapid progress in areas including law and order, infrastructure development, public welfare and cooperation. He observed that Uttar Pradesh has always had a strong social and economic foundation for cooperation. From village chaupals to farms and fields, the tradition of moving forward collectively has remained an integral part of the State’s social fabric, with cooperation providing a modern institutional expression to this spirit. Appreciating the work being undertaken under the leadership of Uttar Pradesh Cooperation Minister Shri J.P.S. Rathore, he highlighted that around 42,000 cooperative societies are presently functioning across the State. He also lauded the Uttar Pradesh Government’s decision to observe 2025 as ‘Sahkarita Mahakumbh’, under which a comprehensive campaign was undertaken to expand the cooperative movement to villages across the State.
Highlighting the success of the M-PACS membership campaign, Shri Mohol stated that more than 54 lakh new members have been enrolled in Uttar Pradesh, including approximately 17.5 lakh farmers. Describing the initiative as a notable example for the cooperative sector across the country, he recalled that Union Home and Cooperation Minister Shri Amit Shah had also appreciated Uttar Pradesh’s membership campaign and recognised its potential as a model that could be considered for replication in other States. The membership campaign has also generated a contribution of around Rs 75 crore for the cooperative sector.
Highlighting Uttar Pradesh’s progress in PACS computerisation, Shri Mohol stated that around 6,300 PACS are being computerised in three phases across the State. In addition, work is being undertaken for the computerisation of approximately 750 agricultural and rural cooperative bank units. Since April 2026, more than 1,200 new M-PACS, dairy, fisheries and other cooperative societies have been formed in Uttar Pradesh, adding approximately one lakh new members. In addition, nearly 22 lakh new members have been enrolled in already operational cooperative societies.
Drawing attention to the growing role of PACS as multipurpose rural service institutions, the Minister noted that around 5,200 Common Service Centres are currently being operated through PACS in Uttar Pradesh. Approximately 7,000 M-PACS are functioning as Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samriddhi Kendras, while 161 M-PACS are providing services as Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras.
Referring to the strengthening of the cooperative banking ecosystem in the State, Shri Mohol highlighted that 16 District Cooperative Banks have been revived with assistance of around Rs 307 crore during the last few years, describing it as an important achievement for Uttar Pradesh’s cooperative sector. Another important milestone has been achieved by the Uttar Pradesh State Cooperative Bank, which has become the first cooperative bank in the country authorised to issue and update Aadhaar cards. In parallel, efforts are also underway towards the establishment of a Cooperative College in Uttar Pradesh to promote study, training and education in the cooperative sector.
Underlining the larger philosophy behind these initiatives, Shri Murlidhar Mohol described cooperation as a powerful means of making the common citizen self-reliant and ensuring dignity for his or her hard work. The expansion of the cooperative model into emerging areas such as mobility, he emphasised, reflects the widening horizons of the movement, with Bharat Taxi representing an important initiative in this direction.
Expressing confidence in the road ahead, Shri Mohol stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the Centre and Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath in Uttar Pradesh, the cooperative movement will continue to expand with greater momentum towards realising the vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’. He further underlined that the cooperative sector will play an extremely important role in realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s resolve of ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’, with continued efforts to bring crores of farmers, workers, youth, women and small entrepreneurs into the mainstream of development through the power of cooperation.

title: Bihar’s Heritage, Folk Traditions and Spiritual Legacy Reflects in 65 PM Mementos
subtitle: Collection brings together Madhubani and Manjusha art, Sikki craft, historical figures and commemorative artefacts
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The cultural richness of Bihar finds expression in a collection of 65 mementos featured in the PM Mementos e-Auction 2026, bringing together the State’s diverse traditions of folk art, handcraft, spirituality, history and heritage. The collection ranges from intricate Madhubani paintings and Sikki craft to representations of revered temples, historical personalities and national symbols.
Rather than representing a single tradition, the collection offers glimpses into the many cultural identities associated with Bihar.
Madhubani and Mithila traditions
A significant part of the collection is devoted to the celebrated Mithila/Madhubani painting tradition. The mementos include depictions of Ram Sita Vivah, Ram Darbar, Chhath Puja, Das Mahavidya and sacred Yantras, along with a Kachni-style Madhubani artwork depicting the Ramayana.
The collection also features several Mithila Paags, hand-painted with traditional motifs such as fish and lotus flowers. The Paag, a distinctive headgear of the Mithila region, is represented through multiple designs and forms.
Craft traditions rooted in the region
Bihar’s craft heritage is also represented through Sikki grass art, including a detailed model of the New Parliament House of India and a traditional woven Sikki basket with integrated coasters. A hand-painted Madhubani artwork on a bamboo winnowing basket combines folk painting with traditional utility craft.
Another distinctive piece is a Manjusha (Angika) painting from Bhagalpur, depicting Bharat Mata against the map of India. Executed in the traditional three-colour palette of yellow, green and red, the work reflects the storytelling tradition of Manjusha art.
History and spiritual heritage
The collection also traverses Bihar’s historical and spiritual landscape. A copper-plate memento depicting Mangal Pandey commemorates the freedom fighter associated with the First War of Independence of 1857. Other artefacts include representations of Ashoka Stambh, Takhat Sri Harmandir Ji Patna Sahib, Lord Buddha, Mahavir Swami and various temples and pilgrimage sites across the State.
Among the religious landmarks featured are Chandika Sthan and Badi Durga Maharani of Munger, Punaura Dham in Sitamarhi, Maa Aranya Devi Temple in Bhojpur, Baba Garibnath Temple in Muzaffarpur, Gorakhnath Dham and Mundeshwari Devi Temple in Kaimur.
The collection further includes mementos associated with  Jan Nayak Karpoori Thakur, Acharya Chanakya and Guru Valmiki, alongside representations of the Ramayana and other cultural traditions.
With base prices ranging from ₹1,500 to ₹1,20,000, the Bihar collection offers collectors an opportunity to engage with the State’s living traditions of art, craft, faith and history through mementos presented to the Prime Minister.
The 8th edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction is live online till October 2, 2026. For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, refer to the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal at:
https://pmmementos.gov.in/#/

title: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurates BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi
subtitle:
India’s BRICS Tax Chairship delivers landmark outcomes across technology, administration and people

Two new India-led Working Groups on International Taxation and Revenue Statistics formally established; BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026 adopted
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated the BRICS Heads of Tax Authorities Meeting in New Delhi today, as the culmination of India’s BRICS Chairship of the tax cooperation track. The meeting was also addressed by the Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of State for Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary, and Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind Shrivastava.
The meeting was attended by Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT, Shri Prasenjit Singh, Member (Legislation), CBDT, other Members of CBDT, and senior officers of the Department of Revenue (DoR). The meeting, hosted by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, brought together the Heads of Tax Authorities of the BRICS member countries. Representatives from ten BRICS tax administrations - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates - came together at one place to share their experiences and discuss emerging challenges through cooperation and collaboration.
In her address on the occasion, Smt. Sitharaman highlighted technology, administration and people as the three recurring themes of BRICS tax cooperation during India’s Chairship. She emphasised the role of data and digital infrastructure in making tax administration more precise and accessible, the importance of durable institutional mechanisms and practical tools that can sustain cooperation beyond individual Chairships, and the value of investing in people and building professional relationships across tax administrations. She also underscored that the perspectives of BRICS economies are essential to ensuring the fairness and durability of ongoing multilateral tax negotiations, including the negotiations on the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation.
The meeting formally adopted several landmark outcomes. Two new Working Groups on International Taxation and Transfer Pricing, and on Revenue Statistics, were established. Both will be led by India, creating sustained institutional platforms that will continue regardless of the Chairship. The first-ever in-person BRICS Young Tax Professionals Capacity Building Programme, held at the National Academy of Direct Taxes, Nagpur in April 2026, was institutionalised as an annual feature of BRICS tax cooperation. The BRICS Tax Cross-Learning Lab was formally launched, integrating the work of the Client-Centric Administration and HR Practices Working Groups into a joint peer-learning platform. The Terms of Reference of the BRICS Tax Support Network was also approved.
The meeting concluded with the formal signing of the BRICS Tax Progress Report 2026, the complete record of India’s Chairship of the BRICS Tax track. The People’s Republic of China was welcomed as the incoming Chair of the BRICS tax cooperation track for 2027.
The Heads of Tax Authorities lauded the Government of India for the successful organisation of the meeting and for the quality and depth of India’s Chairship of the BRICS tax track.

title: Day 2 of IIWW 2026 Brings Diverse Perspectives Together on Water Security, Innovation and Resilient WASH Services
subtitle: From Source Sustainability to AI-Enabled Solutions, IIWW 2026 Technical Sessions Spotlight the Future of Water Management
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second day of the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW 2026) transitioned into its full technical schedule at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, centering on the theme of climate-resilient water management. Organized by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the day featured parallel deliberations across Country, Water Leaders', Practitioners', and Thematic Forums, alongside dedicated side events and the concurrent Second International WASH Conference.
Addressing the Netherland-led Country Forum on “Success Stories in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability”, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena highlighted that India and the Netherlands share a common understanding that water management is not merely an engineering challenge but also a governance, community and climate-resilience challenge. He noted that India’s experience under Jal Jeevan Mission has demonstrated that water security requires strong political commitment, community ownership, scientific planning, accountable institutions and digital innovation working together. He further emphasised that the Mission’s focus is increasingly shifting from infrastructure creation to sustainability, service quality and long-term water security.
Shri Meena also highlighted the growing scope of India-Netherlands cooperation in advancing climate-resilient and sustainable water systems. He referred to initiatives such as the Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure and Decision Support Systems for source sustainability, which support data-driven planning, asset management and risk-informed decision-making. Emphasising the importance of source sustainability, greywater management and local government ownership, he noted that India looks forward to learning from the Netherlands’ extensive experience in water governance while deepening collaboration through research, innovation, capacity building and knowledge exchange.
The technical session on “Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas”, chaired by Ms Aishvarya Singh, Joint Secretary & Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), DDWS highlighted the increasing importance of greywater management in the context of expanding rural water supply coverage. The session brought together State Mission Directors, development partners, Panchayati Raj representatives and grassroots practitioners to share experiences and best practices from different parts of the country, including Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir and Jharkhand.
In her remarks, Ms Singh emphasised that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to greywater management and that solutions must be adapted to local conditions and community needs. The deliberations focused on decentralised treatment and reuse models, integration of greywater management into Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), and strengthening community participation to ensure sustainable water and sanitation outcomes in rural areas.
On the second day of the Second International WASH Conference 2026, six technical sessions were organised on the themes of (i) Digital Technology, AI and Innovation for WASH; (ii) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening; (iii) Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions and Sanitation; (iv) Water Quality, Safety and Emerging Contaminants; (v) Financing, Economic Models and Techno-Economic Solutions; and (vi) Governance, Community Participation and Institutional Strengthening. A total of 25 technical papers were presented, showcasing innovative approaches, emerging research and practical solutions for strengthening climate-resilient and sustainable WASH services.
Technical sessions Details
The first technical session, “Digital Technology, AI & Innovation for WASH,” focused on the use of technology to strengthen the management, monitoring and maintenance of water and sanitation services. Four papers covered a digital communication and monitoring system for rural sanitation in Bihar, a low-cost IoT-based system for on-site detection of heavy metal ions, smart water meters as water-saving devices, and AI-driven decision support for predictive operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems. The presentations highlighted the potential of digital technologies, IoT and AI to improve service monitoring, efficiency and asset management.
The second technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, inclusive approaches and institutional collaboration for sustainable WASH services. Four papers covered a gender-inclusive sanitation model at PCMC, community ownership and digital engagement for rural piped water services in Bihar through the Dastak Abhiyan, inter-departmental collaboration for WASH through the Jal Vidya Programme in Assam, and a service-learning framework for rural sanitation. The session highlighted the role of community ownership, institutional coordination and inclusive approaches in strengthening WASH outcomes.
The third technical session, “Climate Resilience, Nature-Based Solutions & Sanitation/Other,” focused on approaches to strengthening climate resilience and sustainability across water, sanitation and waste management systems. Four papers covered climate adaptation in urban water systems, a cost-effective climate-resilient model for solid waste management, participatory village planning for greywater management, and the application of remotely operated vehicles, AI and sensor technologies for water infrastructure protection and asset management. The session highlighted the role of climate-responsive planning, community participation and technology-enabled approaches in building resilient WASH systems.
The fourth technical session, “Water Quality, Safety & Emerging Contaminants,” focused on approaches to strengthening water quality management and water safety. Five papers examined an integrated approach to safe, energy-independent rural handpump water supply, drinking water quality under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Bongaigaon, Assam, sensor-based detection of water-borne pathogens, community-scale water disinfection technologies, and the use of Jal Jeevan Mission water quality data for seasonal public health risk identification. The presentations highlighted the importance of integrated monitoring, appropriate technologies and data-driven approaches to ensuring safe drinking water.
The fifth technical session, “Financing, Economic Models & Techno-Economic Solutions,” focused on approaches to improving the financial, technological and economic sustainability of WASH services. Four papers covered tablet-based inline chlorination as a cost-effective water safety solution, sustainable approaches to river water filtration and quality assessment, innovative economic models for rural WASH and community sustainability, and the socio-economic assessment of the GOBARdhan component in rural Gujarat. The session highlighted the role of cost-effective technologies, innovative economic models and local capacity building in supporting sustainable water and sanitation services.
The sixth technical session, “Governance, Community Participation & Institutional Strengthening,” focused on community participation, local governance and resilience in WASH service delivery. Four papers examined community participation and social governance in achieving SDG 6 in Rajasthan, the performance of the Swachh Bharat Mission in rural Hoshiarpur, Punjab, approaches to strengthening institutional linkages for flood-resilient WASH systems, and the climate resilience of rural water sources in PESA areas of Himachal Pradesh. The presentations highlighted the importance of community participation, institutional linkages, and locally responsive approaches in strengthening sustainable and climate-resilient WASH systems.
Discussion moved from the opening day's high-level themes into detailed, sector-specific work, spanning water governance and equity, technology adoption and efficiency, climate risk, treated wastewater reuse and community-led recharge. The Thematic Forum opened its paper presentations, across the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes. The sessions drew on the shortlisted papers gathered in the conference proceedings.
COUNTRY FORUM (CF)
CF-2
on
Sharing Technology-Driven Initiatives in Water Security: German and EU Solutions for Sustainable Water Management in India
, was chaired by Mr. Gottfried von Gemmingen, Head of Economic Cooperation & Development at the German Embassy in New Delhi, with GIZ, Siemens, Watershed Monitoring Inc., Asoti Engineering, HUBER Envirotech, and NIVUS Technologies, on digital and precision technologies for water security.
CF-3
on
Success Stories of Countries in Water Management, Food Security and Source Sustainability
, convened with the Netherlands and CEEW was chaired by Mr. Jaap Slootmaker, Vice-Minister of Water & Soil Affairs at the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, Govt. of the Netherlands and co-chaired by Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, IAS, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, discussed circular water economies, climate-resilient agriculture and knowledge transfer.
WATER LEADERS’ FORUM (WLF)
WLF-1 on
Partnership and Cooperation for Inclusive Water Management
, convened with Maharashtra and the World Bank, Drinking Water & Sanitation Department, Jharkhand; IWMI; Development Support Centre, Ahmedabad and Paani Foundation, Maharashtra, was chaired by Dr. Sanjay Belsare, Secretary (CAD), WRD, Maharashtra, and co-chaired by Shri Ajith Radhakrishnan, Senior Water Resources Management Specialist, World Bank, discussed partnership models for water access, quality and resilience across India's agro-climatic regions.
WLF-2 on
Technological Solutions for Efficient Water Utilisation
, convened with FICCI and chaired by Smt. Naina Lal Kidwai, Chair, FICCI Water Mission, FICCI and co-chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary & Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, focused on smart irrigation, digital water management, leak detection and industrial water efficiency.
PRACTITIONERS’ FORUM (PF)
PF-1 on
State Initiatives in Water Management
, was chaired by the Shri Bhopal Singh, Former Member, Central Water Commission, with Shri Zaigam Ali Khan Joint Secretary, NRCD as co-chair, brought together officers and representatives from WRD, Maharashtra; Greater Chennai Corporation; NEIDA; WRD, Madhya Pradesh; and WRD, Haryana, discussed State-level interventions in conservation and service delivery.
PF-2 on
Large-Scale Adoption of Water Saving and Climate-Smart Technology: Lessons from States
, was chaired by Shri Eknath Dawale, IAS, Principal Secretary, WRD, Maharashtra, and Shri Sumant Narain, Joint Secretary, National Water Mission as co-chair on micro-irrigation, solar pumps and digital mapping across Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka and Gujarat.
PF-3 on
Effective Greywater Management for Rural Areas
, convened with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation was chaired by Smt. Aishvarya Singh, JS&MD, SBM(G), DDWS and co-chaired by Shri Brijesh Pandey, Secretary, PWD, Govt. of Tripura on the 3Rs (Reduce, Recharge and Reuse) approach, with about 5.46 lakh villages now having greywater management arrangements; the panel drew in SBM(G) mission directors and grassroots Swachhagrahis and sarpanches.
PF-4 on
Smart Irrigation Management
, was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), Central Water Commission, and co-chaired by Shri Rajeev Kumar, Chief Engineer, UGBO, Central Water Commission. The panelists discussed remote sensing, IoT and AI in irrigation, with IWMI and technology providers.
THEMATIC FORUM (TF)
Eight Thematic Forum sessions ran through the day presenting shortlisted papers and spanning the first three of the Forum's seven sub-themes.
Sub-theme 1, Inclusive and Equitable Water Governance:
TF-1
Equity in Water Allocation and Access to All Sectors
, was chaired by Shri S. Masood Husain, Former Chairman, CWC, and co-chaired by Shri Vineet Gupta, Member, CWMA; TF-2
Water Governance Principles: Indicators, Audit and Standards
, was chaired by Shri B. R. K. Pillai, Professor of Practice, IIT Roorkee, and co-chaired by Dr. P. Somasekhar Rao, Director (Technical), Advanced Centre for Integrated Water Resources Management, Govt. of Karnataka; and TF-3
Institutional Reforms and Strengthening
was chaired by Shri Yogesh Paithankar, Member (WP&P), CWC with Shri Ashish Banerjee, Chief Engineer (IMO), CWC as co-chair. Papers examined equity-based groundwater allocation, women's participation in water governance and the Solar Didi self-help-group model, water auditing and benchmarking of irrigation projects, and parliamentary discourse on river governance.
Sub-theme 2, Collaboration for Optimal Use of Water Resources:
TF-4
Treated Wastewater Reuse Across Sectors
was chaired by Shri Praveen Gupta, Member (Thermal) Central Electrical Authority, with Shri Nalin Kumar Srivastava, Deputy Director General, NMCG as co-chair. TF-
5 Multi-Stakeholder Partnerships for Efficient Water Management
, was chaired by Shri S. K. Haldar, Chairperson, CWMA, with Shri Gopal Kumar, Country Representative, India & Bangladesh, IWMI as co-chair; and TF-6
International Collaboration in the Field of Climate-Related Risk
chaired by Prof. Dr. Deepak Khare, Department of Water Resources Development & Management and co-chaired by Dr. Manish K. Nema, Scientist-E, National Institute of Hydrology, Roorkee. Papers ranged over the circular economy in wastewater, water-sensitive cities, geospatial technologies in the Ken-Betwa link, and drought and flood risk assessment, including a basin-based approach to climate resilience in Kerala.
Sub-theme 3, Technology and Community for Water Security:
TF-
7 Forecasting and Modelling for Water Security
, was chaired by Dr. A. K. Gosain, Professor Emeritus, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Delhi, and co-chaired by Dr. Ajai Pradhan, President & CEO, Cetus Consulting Pvt. Ltd. and TF-8
Community Participation in Groundwater Recharge
, was chaired by Shri Cyril V. Darlong Diengdoh, Commissioner & Secretary, WRD, Govt. of Meghalaya and co-chaired by Dr. Dipankar Saha, Chair Professor, Center for Advanced Water Technology & Management, Manav Rachna University and Board President, Water for People. TF-7 spanned AI, machine learning and remote sensing for water security, SCADA and GIS integration, and flood modelling at river confluences; TF-8 drew on community-led desilting, spring rejuvenation, managed aquifer recharge and the Atal Bhujal Yojana.
SIDE EVENTS (SE)
SE-1 on
Scaling Water-for-Food Solutions in India: Maximising the Impact of PMKSY through Finance, Partnerships and Innovation
, convened by the World Bank with the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), examined how the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana can be strengthened through better financing, stronger partnerships and new innovation to make irrigation water go further for farmers. The session was chaired by Shri Pradeep Kumar Agrawal, Joint Secretary and Chairman, Central Ground Water Authority, and graced by Shri Saroj Jha, Global Director, Water Department, World Bank, who brought a global perspective on financing water security for agriculture.
SE-2 on
GSDP Conversation Series: Accelerating India's Water Vision 2047 through Indo-German Cooperation
, convened by the German Embassy, looked at how the India-Germany partnership can help translate India's long-term water vision for 2047 into practical action on the ground.
H. E. Jasper Wieck, Ambassador, Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, New Delhi, delivered the Inaugural Address. The session was also graced by the august presence of Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, who delivered the keynote address.

title: Indian Railways Connects Remote Area of South Chhattisgarh; Track Reaches Taroki-Rowghat Section of Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Rail Line

date:

content:
Indian Railways achieved a major milestone in the Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Rail Line Project under Raipur Division of South East Central Railway in Chhattisgarh with the completion of final section of the project, Taroki-Rowghat, a single-line electrified broad-gauge section. CRS inspection and speed trial was done on the section yesterday.
The CRS (Commission of Railway Safety) inspection and speed trial are an important process towards the commissioning of the new railway line. During the inspection, the railway line, bridges and culverts, electrification, signalling and other safety and technical arrangements were examined. As per the prescribed procedure, the operational capacity and safety standards of the rail section were also tested.
The Taroki-Rowghat section, covering 17.5 km, is part of the 95 km long Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Line Project and is located at a remote area of south Chhattisgarh. At present, railway services are available to passengers from Dallirajhara to Taroki. Train operations in the Taroki-Rowghat section will strengthen rail connectivity in the surrounding areas and provide better and convenient transportation options to the citizens of the region.
The railway line will facilitate the transportation of iron ore to Bhilai Steel Plant which will give a boost to the steel industry in the country. The railway line will also help in the transportation of  agricultural products and local commercial goods and play an important role in connecting rural and remote areas with the wider railway network. It will significantly enhance connectivity of the region to the capital Raipur as well as to Bhilai which is an educational hub of the state. Hence, improved rail connectivity will facilitate citizens’ access to opportunities related to education, health, employment and trade.
Expansion of rail transport will also promote tourism, investment and other economic activities in the region. This will boost business activities and contribute to the economic and social development of the region.
The inspection and speed trial of the Taroki-Rowghat section mark important progress towards the commissioning of the Dallirajhara-Rowghat New Railway Line Project.

title: Indian Railways Commissions KAVACH 4.0 for the First Time on South Central Railway, Marking a Major Milestone in Railway Safety
subtitle:
KAVACH Upgraded from Version 3.2 to 4.0 on 108 Route Kilometres of Malkajgiri-Kamareddi Section in Hyderabad Division

Enhanced Location Accuracy, Improved Signal Information in Bigger Yards, Station-to-Station OFC Interface and Direct Electronic Interlocking Interface to Strengthen Safety and Reliability
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 12:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Indian Railways has achieved a significant milestone in railway safety with the successful commissioning of KAVACH Version 4.0 for the first time on South Central Railway (SCR). The upgradation from KAVACH Version 3.2 to Version 4.0 has been successfully completed over 108 Route Kilometres on the Malkajgiri-Kamareddi section of Hyderabad Division.
A new boost to rail safety!
KAVACH 4.0 now covers 108 Route Kilometres between Malkajgiri and Kamareddi rail section in Telangana enabling safer and seamless train operations across the region.

The latest version incorporates further technological improvements based on the experience gained from the deployment of KAVACH Version 3.2 over 1,465 Route Kilometres on South Central Railway. KAVACH 4.0 brings enhanced safety, advanced technology, higher reliability and safer train operations, and is planned for large-scale deployment across Indian Railways.
KAVACH 4.0 Brings Advanced Safety Features for India's Diverse Railway Network
KAVACH Version 4.0 has been developed, tested and is now being deployed by Indian Railways as an Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system. The latest version incorporates major improvements required to cater to the diverse operational and technological requirements of the Indian Railways network.
Key improvements in KAVACH 4.0 include:
Increased location accuracy, enabling more precise train positioning.
Improved information of signal aspects in bigger yards, strengthening situational awareness during train operations.
Station-to-station KAVACH interface through Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) for enhanced communication and system integration.
Direct interface with existing Electronic Interlocking Systems, enabling improved integration with existing signalling infrastructure.
These enhancements make KAVACH 4.0 a significant advancement in the country's indigenous Automatic Train Protection technology and provide a strong technological foundation for its large-scale deployment across Indian Railways.
Indigenously Developed KAVACH Enhances Train Safety
KAVACH is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection system designed to enhance operational safety. The system assists the Loco Pilot in maintaining trains within prescribed speed limits and can automatically apply brakes when required if the Loco Pilot fails to do so.
KAVACH is designed to help prevent Signal Passing at Danger (SPAD), control train speed in critical situations and reduce the risk of collisions. The system also supports safer train operations during inclement weather conditions.
As a highly technology-intensive safety system, KAVACH requires safety certification of the highest order, Safety Integrity Level-4 (SIL-4).
Comprehensive Infrastructure Required for KAVACH Deployment
Implementation of KAVACH involves deployment of multiple technological and communication components across railway sections. These include:
Installation of Station KAVACH at stations and block sections.
Installation of RFID tags throughout the track length.
Installation of telecommunication towers throughout the section.
Laying of Optical Fibre Cable along the track.
Provision of Loco KAVACH on locomotives operating on Indian Railways.
The successful commissioning of KAVACH 4.0 on South Central Railway represents an important step towards strengthening indigenous railway safety technology and expanding advanced Automatic Train Protection capabilities across the Indian Railways network.

title: India Shares Experience in Digitisation and Modernisation of Land Records with Sri Lankan Delegation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 SEP 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG). The interaction was held under the chairpersonship of Shri P. Narahari, Joint Secretary, Department of Land Resources, and focused on India’s experience in digitising and modernising land records, with emphasis on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), computerisation of Records of Rights (RoRs), integration of registration with land records and the Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN).
The Sri Lankan delegation was led by Ms. Pathirage Laxman Pathmakumari, Team Leader of the Delegation, Sri Lanka, and included Dr. Mukesh K. Bhandari, Course Coordinator, National Centre for Good Governance, LBSNAA, and Dr. A.P. Singh, Course Director, along with senior officials from Sri Lanka’s land, survey and administrative services.
Welcoming the delegation, Shri P. Narahari highlighted the close ties between India and Sri Lanka and the importance of sharing experiences in public administration. He said, “Land is not merely an administrative record; it is closely linked to livelihoods, economic activity, access to government benefits and citizens’ sense of security. India’s experience has been one of continuously modernising land administration through technology, while recognising the diversity of our States and their land systems. We are pleased to share these experiences with our Sri Lankan colleagues and equally look forward to learning from their institutional practices and reforms.”
During the interaction, Shri Amit Kumar Singh, Director (LR), DoLR, presented an overview of the macro reforms and technological framework powering DILRMP. He highlighted India’s transition from conventional paper-based records to integrated digital land information systems.
Shri Amit Kumar Singh said, “The transformation of land records is not merely about converting paper records into digital form. The larger objective is to create an integrated land information ecosystem where textual records, spatial information, registration data and geospatial technologies complement each other.”
Key DILRMP milestones shared with the delegation included:
99.90% of textual Records of Rights (RoRs) computerised.
97.43% of cadastral maps digitised and 76.16% of land parcels fully georeferenced.
85.24% spatial-textual integration achieved between cadastral maps and RoRs.
40.58 crore+ land parcels assigned the 14-digit alphanumeric Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN).
98.96% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised.
17 States/UTs adopting the centralised National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS), while 17 States operate state-specific digital registration software.
94.11% of Revenue Courts computerised under the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS), enabling real-time litigation marking on property records.
The delegation was also briefed on the integration of cadastral maps and Records of Rights to ensure consistency in ownership details, parcel boundaries and area information.
The interaction covered the integration of property registration with land records through mutation, including ongoing reforms towards paperless registration and automated mutation. Under the emerging system, registration information can be electronically transmitted to the concerned revenue authority for updating land records, reducing delays and the need for repeated visits to government offices.
The delegation was also given a walkthrough of the Bharat Land Stack, an integrated, GIS-based federated architecture bringing together satellite and drone imagery, georeferenced cadastral boundaries, Records of Rights, property registration data, master planning and zoning regulations, building approvals, restrictions and litigation, circle rates and tenancy details. The architecture seeks to provide an integrated digital view of land-related information associated with a parcel.
The visiting officials were further briefed on ULPIN, or Bhu-Aadhaar, which assigns a unique 14-digit alphanumeric identity to land parcels based on their geospatial coordinates. The system facilitates linkage of land parcels with other land-related datasets and maintains linkages when parcels undergo subdivision.
Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal, Director (LR), DoLR, presented a comprehensive overview of the NAKSHA (National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations) programme and its approach to modernising urban land records through advanced surveying and geospatial technologies.
The presentation detailed the end-to-end NAKSHA workflow, including:
Deployment of 2D Nadir cameras, 5-camera Oblique systems and LiDAR sensors mounted on aerial drones for centimetre-level positional accuracy.
Generation of Ortho-Rectified Imagery (ORI), Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and 3D Reality Models for complex urban landscapes.
RTK GNSS rover-based ground truthing, participatory ground validation and transparent claims and objections redressal.
Aerial flying completed across 145 of 150 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) under the pilot phase, progressing towards issuance of legally authentic Urban Property (UrPro) Cards.
Shri Sarvadanand Barnwal said, “NAKSHA is an important step towards strengthening urban land governance through modern geospatial technologies. By creating reliable and integrated urban land records, the programme can support better land administration, improve planning and contribute to greater ease of living for citizens.”
The interaction provided the Sri Lankan delegation with an overview of India’s experience in large-scale land governance reforms, spanning digitisation of land records, spatial-textual integration, digital registration, mutation, geospatial identification of land parcels, computerisation of Revenue Courts and modern urban land mapping.
The engagement underscored the importance of international knowledge-sharing in public administration and highlighted how digital and geospatial technologies can support transparent, integrated and citizen-centric land governance and improve public service delivery.
